title: Metric Gaussian Limits for the Hurwitz Zeta Function and Its Microscopic Analytic Field
content: For Lebesgue-almost every fixed \( \alpha\in(0,1) \), we prove that \( \zeta(1/2+iU_T,\alpha)/\sqrt{\log T} \) converges to the standard circular complex Gaussian law, where \( U_T \) is uniform on \( [T,2T] \). The convergence holds as \( T \) tends to infinity through all real values. We also obtain a microscopic analytic limit with covariance \( \int_0^1e^{-x(z+\overline w)}\,dx \), together with joint limits for all fixed derivative orders. The proof uses martingale differences associated with dyadic partitions of the shift parameter, together with averaging in time. The block Lindeberg condition follows from a uniform spatial \( L^2 \) bound for the nonpermutation part of the multiplicative diagonal in short periodic sums, and from Poisson summation and a metric fourth-moment estimate for long periodic sums. Combining the scalar limit with the fourth-moment bound of Heap and Sahay yields asymptotics for every absolute moment of order 0 < \( p \) < 4.
